messages:
maria: Heads up — helm lint CI started failing on the gpu affinity helpers after #432 merged. It only fails in CI, local `helm template` looks fine.

jason: ugh. any error output from the linter? helm --strict? kubeval?

maria: CI log: `Error: YAML parse error on templates/deployment.yaml: object has no field \"nodeAffinity\"` but the template renders nodeAffinity when values.gpu.enabled=true.

lee: can you paste the helper and the values schema? might be a values.schema.json anyOf issue or the helper returning nil on missing keys.

maria: helper is small:
```tpl
{{- define \"redwood.gpuAffinity\" -}}
{{- if .Values.gpu.enabled }}
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
        - key: cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator
          operator: In
          values:
          - nvidia-tesla-v100
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
```
values.schema.json snippet:
```json
{ "properties": { "gpu": { "type": "object", "properties": { "enabled": { "type": "boolean" } }, "additionalProperties": false } }, "additionalProperties": false }
```

olga: I think the problem is when `include` is used in the Deployment spec and the helper returns nothing helm emits `null` in some contexts which kubeval/helm lint treat as a malformed object. CI runs `helm lint --strict` + `kubeval` on the rendered output. Locally you had `values.gpu.enabled: true` so it never surfaced.

jason: yep. we hit this before with helpers that `return nil` vs `return empty map`. Helm's `include` will insert blank string which can break indentation and the YAML structure. try returning `{}` instead of nothing. e.g. wrap with `- toYaml` and `| nindent` patterns or explicitly return an empty object when disabled.

maria: quick patch I tried:
```tpl
{{- define \"redwood.gpuAffinity\" -}}
{{- if .Values.gpu.enabled }}
  nodeAffinity: ... (same as above)
{{- else }}
  nodeAffinity: {}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
```
That makes lint pass but worried about injecting empty objects into pods that shouldn't have nodeAffinity. Might be fine but feels hacky.

lee: alternative: change usage site. Instead of `{{ include \"redwood.gpuAffinity\" . }}` inline inside `spec.template.spec`, do `{{- with (fromYaml (include \"redwood.gpuAffinity\" .)) }}` and conditionally merge. But `include` already returns string so that gets messy.

olga: values.schema.json `additionalProperties: false` on root + gpu object can also cause `helm lint` validation to complain when we render an empty object somewhere else outside properties. But probably the nil->empty string issue is culprit.

jason: Another robust pattern is to have helper output a YAML block with a comment marker when disabled: `# no-gpu` then use `| nindent` to avoid breaking surrounding structure. But kubeval might still see the key with a comment-only value and complain.

maria: CI runs in a `helm lint` container with Helm v3.11 and kubeval plugin. We've seen this flaky behavior across chart versions. Any recommended canonical pattern?

lee: Our chart library has a `maybeSet` helper we use elsewhere: returns a mapping only when non-empty, otherwise returns nothing but we render it using `include` into a parent map with `toYaml` + `nindent`. Example usage: `{{- if .Values.gpu.enabled }}{{ include \"redwood.gpuAffinity\" . | nindent 8 }}{{- end }}` i.e. guard at usage site. That avoids needing empty objects.

olga: Guarding at site is safest and avoids polluting manifests. But since this chart is consumed by multiple places (cronjob + statefulset + deployment), it's error-prone to update everywhere.

maria: For quick unblock I patched the helper to return `null`-safe minimal map: `nodeAffinity: {}` when disabled; tests passed. But I'll open a follow-up PR to either: 1) update all include sites to be guarded or 2) move affinity into values and let consumers reference `.Values.podAffinity` directly. Thoughts?

jason: Option 2 is cleaner long-term: make affinity a first-class value so non-gpu consumers can override. But it's a breaking change for chart consumers. We can do it in a minor release with migration notes.

olga: Also double-check region constraints: we recently blocked A100 provisioning in us-west1 for cost reasons; if helper assumes `nvidia-tesla-v100` and CI clusters in us-west1 have different labels, tests will pass locally but actual scheduling fails in staging. Add a note in chart README about allowed node labels per region.

maria: good call. I'll: (a) revert to guarded include usage where possible in this chart, (b) add fallback empty map in helper as interim, (c) add README note about region node labels, (d) add a tiny lint test in our pipeline that runs `helm template --values ci.values.yaml` with gpu disabled/enabled matrix.

deploy-bot: CI build #2145 triggered for chart-release/helm-charts@refs/heads/main — lint job retriggered. :gear:

jason: thanks. if anyone hits the same in other charts let's sync and maybe publish a small `chart-helpers` pattern doc. :+1:

maria: I'll open the patch PR now and link here. Thanks all.
